name: WhatsApp AI Agent with Conversation Memory and Human Handoff

parameters.content:
## WhatsApp AI Agent with Conversation Memory & Human Handoff
A WhatsApp agent that actually remembers the conversation. Each WhatsApp message arrives as a separate webhook call with no memory of the last one - this keeps the thread in a sheet keyed by phone number, so the agent stops asking what it was already told.

## How it works
1. Meta POSTs every event to one webhook - most are delivery receipts, not messages, so those are filtered out first
2. The last N turns for that phone number are loaded and the message is logged
3. Three routes:
   - **Needs a human** - they asked for one, or this number was already handed off. The bot stops replying and you get emailed.
   - **Unsupported media** - image, voice note, document. It asks them to type instead of failing silently.
   - **Normal** - AI replies using the conversation history and only the facts you gave it
4. Reply is sent, logged, and the thread stays continuous

## Setup
- [ ] Connect Google Sheets and Gmail credentials
- [ ] Create an httpHeaderAuth credential for Meta: header **Authorization**, value **Bearer YOUR_META_ACCESS_TOKEN**. Attach it to Send WhatsApp Reply.
- [ ] Open Agent Config: Meta phone number ID, business name, handoff email, handoff keywords, history length, and the knowledge base the agent may quote from
- [ ] Create a spreadsheet with a **Conversations** tab and these headers:
      Timestamp, Phone, Name, Direction, Message, Status
- [ ] Point all three Google Sheets nodes at it
- [ ] Activate, then register the production webhook URL in your Meta app under WhatsApp > Configuration

## Customize
Handoff triggers are keywords in config, not code. Raise HistoryTurns for longer memory at the cost of tokens per message.

**Handoff is sticky, and that is deliberate.** Once a number is marked `human` in the Status column, the bot stops replying to it permanently. To hand the conversation back, edit that row's Status to `bot` in the sheet. Without this, a customer waiting on a person keeps getting bot replies over the top of them.

## 1. Intake & Filtering
Meta sends far more delivery/read receipts than actual messages. Anything that is not a real inbound message is dropped here, before it costs an AI call.

## 2. Memory & Routing
This is the part you cannot get from a plain webhook-to-AI setup. History for this phone number is rebuilt from the sheet, the message is logged, then routed three ways.

## 3. Compose, Send, Log
All three routes converge on one send node, so the reply path and logging exist once rather than three times. An empty or failed AI response falls back to a sentence that escalates rather than sending nothing.

## 4. Escalate
You are emailed once, at the moment of handoff - not on every message from that number afterwards.

assignments.name: HandoffKeywords
assignments.value: human, agent, person, manager, complaint, speak to someone

assignments.name: KnowledgeBase
assignments.value:
REPLACE THIS with what the agent is allowed to say. Example:
- Hours: Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm.
- Delivery: 2 to 4 working days.
- Returns: 30 days, unused, receipt required.
- Pricing: starts at $X per month.

parameters.jsCode:
const s = $('Build Conversation State').first().json;
return { json: { phone: s.phone, reply: 'I can only read text messages at the moment. Could you type what you need?', escalated: false } };

parameters.text:
=You are the WhatsApp assistant for {{ $('Agent Config').first().json.BusinessName }}.

What you are allowed to state as fact - nothing outside this:
{{ $('Agent Config').first().json.KnowledgeBase }}

Conversation so far:
{{ $('Build Conversation State').first().json.history }}

Their new message:
{{ $('Build Conversation State').first().json.text }}

Rules:
- WhatsApp length. Two or three sentences, not an email.
- Answer only from the knowledge above. If it does not cover their question, say you will get someone to confirm rather than guessing.
- Do not repeat a question they already answered earlier in the conversation.
- No greeting if the conversation is already underway.
- Plain text. No markdown, no bullet lists.

Reply with the message text only.
